purpose: Find one additional endpoint or provenance family whose curator declares at least four label-independent execution or capture units, while keeping the live REPROD dots.zip acquisition untouched and granting at most a separate metadata-candidate review.

reviewable_direction.why_it_is_reviewable: The curator explicitly declares 63 PANDA traces and defines the source-native capture boundary: each SSH session triggers one 30-second full-system recording. The four Zenodo objects have fixed byte sizes and MD5 values under a versioned CC-BY-4.0 dataset record.

official_capture_declaration.capture_trigger: When an SSH session starts for root, the PANDA recctrl plugin starts a 30-second recording.
official_capture_declaration.source_native_capture_unit: one PANDA trace triggered by one SSH session

associated_publication.title: PANDAcap: A Framework for Streamlining Collection of Full-System Traces
associated_publication.venue: Proceedings of the 13th European Workshop on Systems Security

curator_documentation.repository_description: A framework for streamlining the capture of PANDA execution traces.

evidence_fit.multi_view_lineage_rule: All RR, QCOW, and PCAP material from one SSH session must remain one lineage group and one split.
evidence_fit.candidate_pointer_shape: record DOI + RR archive identity + opaque trace/session identifier + replay event index
evidence_fit.class_balance_implication: The collection is an SSH honeypot/brute-force trace family and does not provide a curator-declared benign/null execution pool.

blocking_risks_before_any_source_role: The record does not declare VM snapshot restoration or equivalent reset between the 63 sessions.
A bounded central-directory audit must prove that at least four stable trace identifiers map to separate non-empty session captures without reading labels or ordinary trace payload.
RR, QCOW, and PCAP views of one SSH session must remain one lineage and one split.
The RRArchive format was described as upcoming and PANDA support as work in progress; no reader identity or reproducible invocation is pinned.
Live honeypot full-system traces, disk deltas, and PCAPs may contain credentials, commands, downloaded payloads, personal identifiers, secrets, or malicious files.
Nested notices and third-party rights inside the archives remain unverified.
The collection has no curator-declared benign/null execution capacity.
Pointer recoverability and protected exact/near-duplicate exclusion remain unverified.

screened_not_advanced.curator_declaration: The official README declares 600 benign and attack scenario graphs with graph IDs 0 through 599 in six scenario-coded ranges.
screened_not_advanced.reason: The repository has strong immutable artifact and license metadata, but graph-ID ranges deterministically encode scenario labels, timestamps were removed during preprocessing, and the README does not declare that each graph is a separately reset or independent source execution. It is retained only as a future derived-graph possibility and does not satisfy this search's stricter label-independent execution key requirement.

The record describes CAPE-generated JSON execution traces for malware samples, but this broad search did not close a source-native one-execution-per-trace manifest, duplicate-run policy, label isolation, reader surface, or metadata-level distinctness. PANDAcap has the stronger explicit session-triggered capture contract.

screened_not_advanced.official_reference: The Zenodo description links Academic Torrents for a VM image and individual samples.
screened_not_advanced.reason: The reviewable candidate is pinned only to Zenodo record revision 4 and its four MD5-addressed objects. Mirrors, torrents, standalone VM images, and individual samples are not substituted into the artifact Gate.

supports: four file byte sizes and MD5 values
one recording triggered by each SSH session
RR/QCOW/PCAP layout and same-session view relationship

matrix.source: StreamSpot official project web page linked from its repository

conflict_of_interest.effect_on_independence_claim: The same team curates the framework, dataset record, and documentation, so reset and uniqueness claims still require artifact-level audit.

verification_limitations: No archive, archive member, trace, disk image, PCAP, ordinary repository code, paper full text, model output, or protected payload was read.
The official metadata declares session-triggered captures but does not publish a machine-readable one-trace-per-session manifest at the record level.
Statistical independence, VM reset, duplicate sessions, pointer recoverability, nested notices, privacy isolation, and protected exclusion require separately authorized bounded audits.
The StreamSpot project web page returned HTTP 403; its official GitHub README, repository license, immutable tree, and Crossref paper record were sufficient only for a hold decision.

evidence: Zenodo revision 4 and DataCite agree on PANDAcap dataset DOI, title, creators, version 1.0, Dataset type, open access, and CC-BY-4.0 rights.
The Zenodo record publishes four objects totaling 22433496290 bytes and an MD5 for every object.
Zenodo and the pinned curator document both declare 63 PANDA traces and state that each SSH session triggers one 30-second PANDA recording.
The same documentation states that RR, QCOW disk-delta, and PCAP files are views of the same 63 sessions.
Crossref verifies the matching-author ACM EuroSec 2020 paper, and Zenodo formally marks the dataset as its supplement.
No metadata source declares VM reset, a one-trace-per-session immutable manifest, duplicate-session policy, or a safe RRArchive reader identity.
inference: PANDAcap is a stronger fit than StreamSpot for this search because its source-native capture boundary is a live SSH session recording, not merely a derived graph count.
The capture grouping rule is label-independent at the metadata level: one session triggers one trace, without using attack family, technique, verdict, file count, or time window to create groups.
The 63 traces remain candidate capture groups rather than verified independent lineages because reset, duplicate, manifest, and statistical-independence Gates are open.
RR, QCOW, and PCAP are multiple sensor or state views of the same sessions and must never be counted as separate families or lineages.
Full-system honeypot traces are scientifically relevant but carry unusually high privacy, secrets, malware, dual-use, reader, and pointer risks.
recommendation: Approve only a separate metadata-candidate review for pandacap_ssh_honeypot_full_system_traces_2020; do not write the effective catalog, assign a source role, or award family, lineage, sample, or quota credit.
A future per-family review should prefer eurosec2020-pandacap-rr.zip as the only endpoint/provenance surface under consideration and keep QCOW and PCAP excluded by default.

If that review passes, require a new exact bounded acquisition contract, a reader/tool amendment for RRArchive, central-directory and nested-notice caps, privacy/secret/malware isolation, session manifest and multi-view binding, pointer probe, and protected exact/near exclusion.
Fail closed if four stable session traces cannot be proven without reading labels, sensitive session content, disk deltas, PCAP payload, or hidden ground truth.
